messages:
aria: FYI — after the kernel + driver push last night, ~12% of eu-west p4 nodes started failing NVML init and pods are stuck in ImagePullBackOff for CUDA images. noticed around 02:12 UTC.

sam: @aria can you paste the node errors? any stacktraces?

aria: logs from one node: `nvidia-smi: initialization error: driver not loaded` then kubelet churn: `container runtime error: could not find libnvidia-ml.so`. Also dmesg shows `nvidia: unknown symbol nvidia_pci_init`.

dena: sounds like a kernel/driver ABI mismatch to me. which kernel version rolled?

aria: We rolled to 6.4.12 and pushed nvidia-driver-535.70.03 + cuda-12.1 runtime yesterday (eu-west canary = 8 nodes).

leo: If NVML symbols missing -> driver module probably built against older kernel ABI. Might be DKMS vs packaged module mismatch.

nina: Affected nodes are in two host pools: eu-west-gpu-ondemand and eu-west-dedicated-reserved. Dedicated has some reserved capacity that can't be moved easily.

tal: Priority = keep production alive. Proposal: immediate package hold for drivers on eu-west-dedicated, roll back the canary, and gate any further kernel upgrades until we have a compatibility matrix.

aria: Agree. Also observed increased cross-host NCCL connection failures after partial node restarts. Probably related.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-2145 — GPU drivers failing post-kernel-upgrade in eu-west. Pager notified: @eng-oncall.

sam: Steps I'm doing now: 1) cordon+drain two affected nodes in canary; 2) boot one node into previous kernel (6.3.x) and test `nvidia-smi`; 3) snapshot node images.

dena: For the hold: apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 libcudnn8 && record in infra-deployments repo. For rpm hosts use `yum versionlock add` — add these to the holdlist script.

aria: Sharing quick snippet for ops playbook:

```
# hold apt packages (debian/ubuntu)
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535 cuda-toolkit-12-1
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 cuda-toolkit-12-1
# rpm (rhel/centos)
sudo yum install -y kmod-nvidia-535 cuda-12.1
sudo yum versionlock add kmod-nvidia-535 cuda-12.1
```

leo: Also add node annotation `redwood/gpu-driver:locked-535-12.1` so automation knows not to upgrade those pools.

nina: We need a regional gating matrix in the repo: columns = region, kernel, driver, libcudnn, nccl, status. I'll put a draft PR to infra-playbooks.

sam: Can we fallback to a soft-degraded path — route latency-sensitive traffic to us-east for the next 6h? That'll cost reserved cross-region egress but saves customer-facing latency SLOs.

tal: Approve routing shift for 6h. Notify SRE + Growth for cost heads-up.

aria: Rolling back canary state: created rollback image `ami-gpu-20260318-v2` and started replacing canary nodes. If `nvidia-smi` green, we'll gradually replace dedicated nodes but leave hold in place.

dena: Long term: we need an automated kernel-driver compatibility test matrix in CI that runs on each node-type, with DKMS build verification and a quick NCCL smoke-test (allgather + simple gbench).

leo: I'll add a kube preflight job that runs on new node images: `modprobe nvidia && nvidia-smi && run-nccl-smoke`. If it fails, block image publish.

nina: PR to infra-playbooks created: https://git.redwood/infra-playbooks/pulls/142 — contains holdlist script, regional matrix CSV, and node-annotation automation.

sam: For communication: posting incident note to #incidents and sending a short status update to @product and @support.

tal: Postmortem owners: sam + dena. Timeline: incident start 02:12 UTC, rollback initiated 02:35 UTC, canary healthy 03:10 UTC, holdlist applied 03:25 UTC.

aria: Final ask: everyone, if you touch driver/kernel packaging today, please ping `#eng-infra` and link the compatibility matrix. We'll keep deploy freeze for kernel+driver changes in eu-west until PR merged. :locked:

deploy-bot: Deploy blocked: kernel/driver changes to eu-west until infra-playbooks PR #142 merge and CI gates pass.

sam: Thanks — I'll update the incident and kick off the postmortem doc.

aria: Good work team. We'll reconvene after the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
